title: Bounded-metric eviction orchestrator for KV cache: prefix-aware LRU/TTL with correctness contracts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As throughput increases with continuous batching, KV cache pressure on GPU memory grows non-linearly. Existing heuristics (pure LRU or simple TTL) either over-evict hot prefix slices used by batched requests or under-evict noisy cold keys leading to OOMs and tail latency spikes. Goal: design and ship a bounded-metric eviction orchestrator that combines prefix-aware LRU with TTL and watermarking so eviction decisions are provably safe for correctness (no returned stale keys, no KV footprint races with in-flight batch inference) while optimizing for GPU footprint and batch latency. The orchestrator must integrate with continuous batching (request coalescer and slot manager), support lease-backed invalidation handshakes, and expose metrics for SLOs and auditing.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-tier eviction orchestrator: 1) soft-watermarks per-GPU slab that trigger advisory trimming using an age-weighted LRU factoring prefix affinity and recent batch coaccess; 2) hard-watermarks that drain using TTL-pruning + lease-fencing ensuring in-flight batches hold eviction tokens until safe. Eviction operations are recorded to a compact ledger so rollbacks (on memory reclaim failures) are deterministic. Provide a lightweight runtime API for batching to acquire & release leases when pinning prefixes during continuous batched inference. Provide correctness contracts and a validation harness (fuzz + replay) to show zero-return-of-evicted-prefix during steady-state and during failover.
design_decisions: Use per-prefix counters to bias LRU so multi-request hot prefixes survive trimming
Lease-based pinning: batches acquire short-lived leases that prevent eviction until batch completion or lease expiry
Two watermarks: soft (advisory) to trigger prefetch/prioritize demotion, hard to force atomic invalidation with fencing
Eviction ledger: append-only compact record for audit and deterministic replay in the validation harness
Integrate with existing slot allocator: when a slot is assigned, it checks lease API rather than directly touching KV entries
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Initial spec drafted; outlined soft/hard watermark semantics and lease handshake
2026-02-23: Design review with runtime and infra; SRE flagged observability gaps and rollback story
2026-03-01: Prototype implemented in local runtime branch: lease API + in-memory eviction ledger
2026-03-05: Synthetic perf runs with simulated continuous batching show 18% reduction in OOM events under bursty prefix distributions
2026-03-10: Found race related to race between lease expiry and batch commit when network jitter introduced; added lease-extension path and atomic commit token
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes lease acquire/release API and batching runtime uses it to pin prefixes
Eviction ledger persisted for each eviction action with (timestamp, prefix, slot, reason)
No observed return-of-evicted-prefix in the validation harness across 1M randomized replayed sequences
End-to-end tests that simulate network jitter and worker restarts pass without returning stale keys
Metrics: reduce OOM-triggered restarts by >= 15% in bursty synthetic workload; maintain median batch latency change <= 5%
Documentation updated: SDK contract, admin knobs (soft/hard watermark %), and operational runbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease API covering normal, expiry, and extension paths
Integration test: batch runtime pins prefixes and completes while eviction aggressor runs concurrently
Fuzz harness: generate 1M random sequences of acquire/release/evict with a verified model of correctness to assert no returned-evicted
Chaos tests: introduce pause during ledger write to simulate transient storage errors and validate rollback behavior
Perf sweep: evaluate soft/hard watermark thresholds for cost/latency trade-offs across 4 workload shapes (uniform, zipf-hot-key, prefix-skew, bursty-spike)
risks: Lease churn overhead could add per-batch latency if not amortized by slot coalescing
Ledger persistence must be extremely lightweight; otherwise we risk tail latency and additional GPU host CPU pressure
Mis-tuned watermarks can either cause under-eviction (OOM) or over-eviction (increased token generation cost)
Complexity of integration with existing autoscaler and model-variant fallback routing could create edgecases
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy to a single non-critical region; enable soft-watermark advisory only; run validation harness against live traffic mirror
Phase 1: Enable lease-based pinning for small percentage (5%) of requests and soft trims active; monitor OOMs and latency
Phase 2: Enable hard-watermark enforcement for half of canary hosts with aggressive ledger retention disabled (ephemeral), verify correctness
Phase 3: Full rollout with ledger retention enabled, add admin knobs to console and set default conservative watermarks
notes: SRE recommends exposing a debug trace header so request traces can be correlated with ledger entries
We should amortize lease RPCs by batching lease grants per slot allocation to reduce host IPC
Consider a future follow-up to integrate quantized footprint estimates to prioritize evictions by actual GPU memory bytes rather than entry counts
